questions.question:
**Select the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, mark ‘No error’.**

The terrorist members of Lashkar-e-Taiba attacked on the Taj Hotel in November 2008.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 2) i.e. 'attacked on the Taj Hotel.'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in the part 'attacked on the Taj Hotel.'
 
• According to the rules of prepositions, no preposition is used after certain verbs when the sentence is in active voice.
 
• Here the verb **'attacked' ** is such an exceptional verb.
 
• Therefore we need to **omit 'on' after the verb** to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 

Correct sentence:__ *The terrorist members of Lashkar-e-Taiba **attacked the Taj Hotel** in November 2008.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The list of such verbs after which preposition is not used in active voice

 
 
• **ensure, demand, board, stress, resemble, comprise, direct, concern attack, invade, investigate, succeed, sign, describe, resist, befall, emphasise, pervade, affect, accompany, consider, order, regret, await, violate, lack, precede, discuss, join.**

questions.question:
**Choose the appropriate word to complete the given sentence.**

The news was _______ good to be true.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"too".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "Too" is used to indicate that something is more than what is wanted, needed, or considered as acceptable.
 
• It's often used before an adjective or adverb to express an excessive or overwhelming degree of a certain quality.
 
• In this particular case, **'too' **implies that the news is so good that it's hard to believe or accept as true.
 
• Given these explanations, the most appropriate word to complete the sentence is **"too". **
 
• It helps to express the idea that the goodness of the news exceeds what one can easily believe or accept.
 
• So, the correct sentence would be: "The news was too good to be true."

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "very" - This word is used to emphasize an adjective, adverb, or a phrase.
 
 
• In this context, 'very' would stress how good the news is but wouldn't imply any consequence or express doubt or disbelief.
 
 
 
• "so" - This word is used to emphasize an adjective or an adverb, similar to 'very'.
 
 
• However, it doesn't express the idea of excess or being beyond what is good or acceptable.
 
 
 
• "as" - This word is typically used in comparisons and it would not make sense in this context since it's not comparing the goodness of the news to anything else.

questions.question:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to improve it, select 'No improvement'.

__As such you missed__ the last program, here is a summary of the story.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3), i.e., 'In case you missed.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in Part **(As such you need)** of the sentence.
 
• A conjunction is a word which is used to connect clauses or sentences or to coordinate words in the same clause.
 
• **'In case'** means **'if it is true that**'.
 
 
• *Example:** In case** you haven't figured it out, let me explain.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, in the erroneous part, the use of 'As such you missed' in the sentence should be replaced with 'In case you missed' to make it grammatically correct.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Correct sentence:__ ***__In case you missed__** the last program, here is a summary of the story.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to improve it, select 'no improvement required'.**

The first step __in making a kite is to fasten__ two sticks of bamboo together in the form of a cross.

options.text: in making a kite is to be fastened
in making a kite is to fastening
into making a kite is fasten

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **no improvement required**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The infinitive '**to fasten' **has been used correctly.
 
• Infinitives are a form of the verb that allow the word or a group of words to be used as a **noun, adjective, or adverb**. 
 
• **'In making' **is also used correctly.
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct in all aspects.
 
• Hence, the most appropriate answer is **option 4**.
 
• The correct sentence is **The first step in making a kite is to fasten two sticks of bamboo together in the form of a cross.**

questions.question:
Select the option which gives the nearest meaning of the idiom/phrase.

To let the chips fall where they may

options.text: To let something happen regardless of consequences

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'To let something happen regardless of consequences.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase "to let the chips fall where they may" comes from the world of logging, where "chips" are the pieces of wood that fly when a woodsman cuts a tree.
 
• The saying has come to mean to let events unfold naturally, without interference, and to accept the outcome, whatever it may be.
 
• 'To let something happen regardless of consequences' (option 2) perfectly captures the spirit of the idiom.
 
• **It suggests a willingness to let events unfold as they may, without trying to control the outcome.**

Thus, **option 2 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The time spent/in capturing photos/can act like an alternative therapy/to help to uplift one's mood.

options.text: can act like an alternative therapy
to help to uplift one's mood

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "to help to uplift one's mood".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Here, the use of two consecutive 'to' is unnecessary and grammatically incorrect. While both 'to help' and 'to uplift' make sense when used separately, combining them creates redundancy.
 
• Hence, the correct phrase should either be 'to help uplift one's mood' or 'to uplift one's mood'.
 
• This removal of the unnecessary usage of 'to' resolves the redundancy and enhances the sentence's conciseness without changing its meaning.

Therefore, the corrected sentence would be: "The time spent in capturing photos can act like an alternative therapy to help uplift one's mood."

Thus, the correct answer is "option 3".

questions.question:
**Directions: **In these question, which of the phrases (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below each sentence should replace the phrase printed in CAPITAL LETTERS to make the sentence grammatically correct?

FINISHING HIS BREAKFAST, he started working on the problem that had been awaiting disposal for a longtime.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Having finished his breakfast". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **'FINISHING HIS BREAKFAST' **implies the action is ongoing which is contradicting with the later part of the sentence where he has already started to work on the problem.
 
• The correct phrase should be in a form in which the action of finishing breakfast has been completed.
 
• **'Having finished his breakfast' **is the right phrase, as it clearly states that the action is complete before he starts working on the problem.
 
• The use of **'having' **indicates the completion of previous action and the commencement of a new one.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 3". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 (His breakfast finished) is passive-voice and does not clarify who performed the action.
 
• Option 2 (His breakfast having finished) is grammatically incorrect due to the unusual and incorrect structure.
 
• Option 4 (Finished his breakfast) is a clause that does not fit appropriately in the sentence's context.

questions.question:
Arrange the parts(1), (2), (3) and (4) of the following sentences to create meaningful sentences and choose the right option accordingly.

1) people think they're

2) Blackberry phones used to be

3) old-fashioned gadgets

4) extremely popular, but now many
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**2, 4, 1, 3**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The part '**2**' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving information about the **noun **'*Blackberry phones*' that *earlier they used to very popular but with the passage of time, people are considering them old fashioned gadgets*. Hence, '2' is the first part.
 
• The phrase '*extremely popular*' mentioned in the part '4' refers back to the noun '*Blackberry phones*' mentioned in the part '2'. Hence, '4' follows '2'.
 
• The noun '*people*' mentioned in the part '1' is linked with the phrase '*but now many*' mentioned in the part '4'. Hence, '1' follows '4'.
 
• The sentence '3' is the concluding sentence. Hence, '3' is the last sentence.
 
• The correct sequence is 2, 4, 1, 3.

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences:- *Blackberry phones used to be extremely popular, but now many people think they're old-fashioned gadgets.*

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase **"such as"** is used to introduce examples that clarify or illustrate what has been mentioned before.
 
• The other options **("for as," "from as," "same as")** do not appropriately introduce examples in this context.
 
• **"Such as" **fits perfectly here as it introduces examples of different pedagogical approaches **(experiential learning, arts-integrated, sports-integrated, and storytelling-based approaches).**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1 (such as)**.

 

***Correct Sentence:*** *"Teachers will be given continuous opportunities for self-improvement and to learn the latest innovations and advances in their professions. Each teacher will be expected to participate in at least 50 hours of CPD opportunities every year for their own professional development, driven by their own interests. CPD opportunities will, in particular, systematically cover the latest pedagogies regarding foundational literacy and numeracy, formative and adaptive assessment of learning outcomes, competency-based learning and related pedagogies, **such as** experiential learning, arts-integrated, sports-integrated and storytelling-based approaches, etc."*
